history.summary: Historic Vaishnavite temple on Harimandir Road in Dharmanagar market, North Tripura — 'Hari' is a name of Vishnu, and Janmashtami (Krishna's birth) is celebrated here with special puja, arati, kirtan and Bhagavad Gita recitations (Tripura Star News, September 2026). IDENTITY CAVEAT: one map/listing service marks this location 'permanently closed', but a September 2026 local news report shows Janmashtami being actively celebrated at the Harimandir in Dharmanagar market — the temple appears to be active, and the closed listing looks stale. Deity specifics, founding date and opening hours are unverified (verify locally).

name: Hari Mandir, Dharmanagar
town_description: Dharmanagar is the headquarters of North Tripura district, a municipal town near the Assam border in the northernmost part of the state; it is Tripura's second town by road/rail connectivity after Agartala and a gateway to the Jampui Hills and Unakoti.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~180–200 km) or Silchar Airport, Assam (~120 km)
travel.railway: Dharmanagar railway station; trains connect Silchar and Agartala
travel.road: Silchar–Dharmanagar ~120 km (~3 hours); Agartala–Dharmanagar ~200 km (~8–9 hours)

visitor_information.best_time: Janmashtami (August/September) for the main festival; otherwise the cooler dry months (October–March)
